candidates.change_summary: Removed the onlyAdmin modifier from setOwner so any caller can change owner, allowing different owner after call.
Change assignment to set admin instead of owner inside setOwner so owner remains unchanged after call.
Assign the zero address to owner inside setOwner, making owner different after call regardless of _owner.
Invert the onlyAdmin check so non-admins can call functions using onlyAdmin but the admin cannot, changing whether setOwner can succeed and thus owner.
Change setOwner to return false instead of true after setting owner.
Make setOwner return the zero/non-zero check of the new owner address (returns false if address(0), true otherwise) instead of always true.

Modify onlyAdmin to always allow (remove require) so setOwner can be called by any caller and still return true in original, but here we change to return false via changing setOwner to check admin — instead we change onlyAdmin to always succeed; combined with original setOwner this allows different callers but return remains true; however this mutant focuses on altering authorization behavior which can produce differing observable results for some callers. (only the modifier body is changed to no require)
Remove the onlyAdmin modifier requirement by deleting the modifier on the function, allowing anyone to call setOwner and change owner.
Require that the caller is the current owner instead of the admin, changing who can successfully call setOwner.
Change the onlyAdmin modifier to require msg.sender equals owner (not admin), so calls passing onlyAdmin will be allowed only for owner, altering who can call setOwner.
Make setOwner always revert by adding a require(false), preventing owner from ever being changed via this function.
